clue.text: Exotic cher — cheer wildly!

indicators.note: letters treated wildly are thrown about into a new order, so the two words are mixed up together

explanation.surface: A fan urges the crowd to give the glamorous singer Cher a rousing cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' shuffles the letters of CHER and CHEER together; 'cher' looks like the singer's name or the French for dear, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recherché is rare, choice and carefully sought out, hence exotic or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Rise with difficulty, taking posture of defiance

indicators.note: the word rise, managed only with difficulty, comes out with its letters awkwardly rearranged

parts.note: a posture is a stance, the way one stands

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to their feet and strikes a defiant pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges RISE into RESI, which 'taking' joins to STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is opposition or refusal to give in, a synonym of defiance.

clue.text: Silly person takes cocaine

explanation.surface: A foolish individual starts using hard drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a fool, and it is also street slang for cocaine, from the C.

clue.text: Bottom of the lake is weird

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of the

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Something strange lurks at the bottom of the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' applies to the word 'the', not to the lake bed, giving E before ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, close to weird or uncanny.

annotationWithheld.clue: Tineid found by the loch, most unusually

clue.text: Animal by Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A creature is found grazing beside a loch in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a farm animal, and Loch Ewe is a sea loch in the north-west Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Leave a car with a cover plus hood attachment

parts.note: to park is to leave a car standing somewhere

explanation.surface: Instructions to park the car and put a cover with an attached hood over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a car cover with a bonnet fitting, but it describes a hooded jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a weatherproof jacket with an attached hood, so a covering garment with a hood fixed on.

clue.text: Sponge a last diver, north of pier, set adrift

annotationWithheld.why: Sponge a last diver, north of pier, set adrift (9): held answer PORINERAN is not a word; anagram of A + R + N + OF + PIER gives PORIFERAN. Letter 5 crosses the corrupt 11-across row (stray T shift), so answerTypo is refused.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sponge a last diver, north of pier, set adrift

clue.text: Cardinal keeps under surveillance a number of rudd

annotationWithheld.why: Cardinal keeps under surveillance a number of rudd (3,4): held answer REDELES is not a word; RED + EYES gives REDEYES. Letter 5 crosses the corrupt 11-across row (stray T shift), so answerTypo is refused.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cardinal keeps under surveillance a number of rudd

clue.text: Upturn for key health resort, this recess

indicators.note: upturn in a down clue means the word is turned to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a spa is a health resort with mineral springs
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A recovery at a spa town is being presented as the place for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upturn' sounds like an economic recovery but reverses SPA to APS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Heavenly body I see in flight

indicators.note: I is seen in the heavenly body, so the letter is placed inside that word

parts.note: a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Someone spots a star or planet moving through the sky in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests flying, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish and older usage a stair can mean a whole set of steps, i.e. a flight.

clue.text: Countermands orders I've circulated

indicators.note: letters circulated are passed around and so end up in a new order

explanation.surface: An officer cancels instructions that have already gone round the department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' sounds like memos going round an office, but it is the anagram signal working on the two words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To countermand an order is to cancel it with a superior instruction, setting it aside.

clue.text: Scrambling over ferny hills, point out this insect

annotationWithheld.why: Scrambling over ferny hills, point out this insect (10,3): held answer SILVERTHORNFL is not a word; OVERFERNYHILLS less E (point) gives SILVERHORNFLY. The held row has a stray T after the sixth letter shifting the rest one square (corrupting crossings 4d, 6d, 7d, 12d); 7 letters differ, beyond answerTypo's limit.
annotationWithheld.clue: Scrambling over ferny hills, point out this insect

clue.text: Freeze, with a tiger free? Run inside! Set off!

annotationWithheld.why: Freeze, with a tiger free? Run inside! Set off! (11): held answer OEFRIGERATE is not a word; anagram of A TIGER FREE with R inside gives REFRIGERATE. Letter 1 crosses the corrupt 11-across row (stray T shift), so answerTypo is refused.
annotationWithheld.clue: Freeze, with a tiger free? Run inside! Set off!

clue.text: Brushes to convey — lots here

parts.note: sweeps are strokes of a brush, so brushes stands for sweeps
to take something is to convey or carry it

explanation.surface: Someone carries brooms and brushes, and plenty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like a large quantity, but it means lots drawn in a lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: In this gamble the prize money goes to holders of tickets drawn by lot.

clue.text: Approaches made as meeting place entered

indicators.note: the meeting place has entered the word as, so it goes between its letters

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: People draw near as soon as a meeting place has been reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are routes or ways towards something, i.e. approaches, as in avenues of inquiry.

clue.text: What, doubtless, you are not

parts.note: read as a riddle: someone free of doubt cannot be the opposite state, doubtful or undecided

explanation.surface: A confident remark about something you surely are not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubtless' reads as 'surely', but it describes the person: someone without doubts cannot be its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without doubts is sure, the opposite of being doubtful or undecided.

clue.text: Following warning cry, was turning tail as anticipated

indicators.note: following means the next piece comes after the warning cry in the answer

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning that a ball is coming

indicators.note: turning tail means turning round, so the word was is read backwards

explanation.surface: After a golfer's shout, someone fled, just as had been expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' looks like running away, but it means turning round; 'fore' is the shout a golfer gives to warn people ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see something coming beforehand, i.e. to anticipate it.

clue.text: Spirit of the Caribbean

parts.note: a liqueur flavoured with bitter orange peel and named after an island of the Dutch Caribbean

explanation.surface: The essence or soul of the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a soul or atmosphere, but it is an alcoholic drink, named after the island it comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-flavoured liqueur takes its name from a Dutch Caribbean island where its bitter oranges grow.

clue.text: Concerned over height of river, find us fresh living quarters

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: re means concerning, about, so concerned stands for it
the Ouse is an English river, one of several of that name

explanation.surface: Worried about rising river levels, a family asks to be moved to a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerned' looks like worried but gives RE (about); 'over' puts RE above H in this down entry; the Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse people is to provide them with new accommodation.

clue.text: Sadly, I belong in a lower category

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters of belong are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Someone laments that they belong in a lesser class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' reads as regret but rearranges BELONG into GNOBLE, set after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble originally meant of humble birth, i.e. of a low social rank.

clue.text: Dub ruin's rebuilding fitting for place in Africa

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the letters of the ruin back together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Restoring a ruined building in Dub is a suitable project for somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' rearranges DUB RUIN (the 's is no letter); 'fitting for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Burundi is a small landlocked country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Draconian procedure utilised by us harms English hares

definitions.note: the definition is singular but describes a policy made up of several steps, which the plural answer names

indicators.note: the letters utilised are put to new use, rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A severe policy we adopt is harming English hares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utilised' rearranges US HARMS E HARES; the surface pictures a cruel cull of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively severe, after the Athenian lawgiver Draco, so it names severe steps taken.

clue.text: Writer climbing a tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer and Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: An author scrambles up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns CAMUS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree of the cashew family.

clue.text: A continental company's strange in Scotland

parts.note: un is French for a, the article a continental would use
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A European firm is considered odd by the Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' means European, here French, where 'a' is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is a Scots word meaning odd or unusual.

clue.text: Shooting pains, due to deployment of aerial gun

indicators.note: the deployment of letters spreads them out into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sharp pains are blamed on firing an anti-aircraft gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployment of' rearranges AERIAL GUN; 'Shooting' ties in with the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is intense, stabbing pain along the course of a nerve.

clue.text: Open space needed for making a park

definitions.text: Open space needed for making a park

parts.words: Open space needed for making a park
parts.note: read not as laying out parkland but as parking a car, which needs an empty slot between other vehicles

explanation.surface: Land must be set aside before a public park can be created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a park' suggests landscaping a public park, but it means parking a car in a space.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty space or opening between things, such as between parked cars.

clue.text: Disorder apparent when I first arrived on a British isle

indicators.note: in an across clue, arrived on means coming after the British isle

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: first means the letter I comes before the letter a

explanation.surface: Chaos broke out when I first landed on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrived on' puts IA after MAN; the Isle of Man sits between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is a mental disorder of excessive excitement and elation.

clue.text: On reflection, act one needs changing, for the theatre

indicators.note: on reflection, as in a mirror, means the word for act is read backwards

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: the word one needs changing, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a director decides act one must be rewritten for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' looks like thinking it over but reverses DO; 'needs changing' rearranges ONE to EON.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was a building for music in ancient Greece, and the name later went to a cinema chain.

clue.text: Doctor may do so before the writer

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a scribe is a writer, someone who copies documents

explanation.surface: A doctor might do this ahead of the person writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer' usually means ME in crosswords, but here it is SCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors write out orders for medicines, which is what this verb means.
